research_concepts: teammate DRIVE preceding PNR within a possession
play-type labeling from play-by-play and initiator records
sequential play-type premiums (teammate and same-player sequences)
label validation and foul leakage in derived play types
methodological_questions: Does a teammate DRIVE immediately before a PNR raise PNR PPP relative to matched PNR possessions without that sequence?
Are the PNR and DRIVE labels valid enough to define the sequence without systematic misclassification?
How much of any sequence effect is confounded by shooter quality, defensive matchup, lineup, score, clock, and possession context?
Can a placebo or falsification sequence separate a real sequence effect from labeling or construction artifacts?

historical_evidence.finding: Team-level RS vs playoff comparison found DRIVE PPP 1.198 RS vs 0.912 PO (-0.286, 25 teams) and PNR -0.173. This is a play-type context effect, not a teammate-sequence test, and it reports no CIs.

Foul leakage: OTHER possessions ended in fouls 36% of the time with PPP inflated; DRIVE was 12pp below the foul benchmark; PNR showed a 22% foul rate; only 335 of 50,668 possessions (0.7%) mapped to a real play type via initiation_type.

Play-type label accuracy audit with overall FAIL: OTHER 20.2% vs <10% target; 40.8% low confidence; DRIVE foul-draw 1.7% vs 14-22% benchmark; most PT PPP above benchmark band; MIA identity checks failed.

Label backfill verification finished FAIL: PNR 28.7% (band 20-28%) FAIL; PULL_UP 7.9% FAIL; 82.8% of PNR labels proxy_calibrated; PNR PPP 0.948 PASS; team identity FAIL; 2024-25 PULL_UP shares 0-2% for many teams.

Assisted-flag leak: SPOT_UP showed 2.83 PPP and TRANSITION 0.62 PPP because the assisted flag exists only on makes; after rewrite SPOT_UP was about 1.16 and TRANSITION about 1.20. Demonstrates that PPP by inferred type can be manufactured by the labeling construction.
On-ball coverage labels: confident label rates 14.9% (DET, 10 of 67) and 3.3% (ORL, 2 of 60); switches_on not populated by the NBA matchups feed. Failed gate.
Pooled series-bucket PPP showed no clear DRIVE signal across playoff series (DRIVE 0.889 to 0.949, +0.060); recorded as selection or regression-to-the-mean limited, with no CIs.
Defensive PPP allowed and share RS vs playoffs by play type: DRIVE allowed 1.191 to 0.923; PNR share +12.1pp, which the record says may reflect tagging differences.

Shot-level PNR shares by team (2024-25) ranged from about 7.6% (OKC) to 13.8% (IND); calibrated possession-level PNR later reported at about 17.9-19.6%, indicating the share depends on the labeling pipeline. No validation recorded.

Sequential premiums: same-player DRIVE to PNR cells show opposite signs (L. Doncic +0.309, n=53; D. Bane -0.324, n=70, t=-2.7); teammate sequence cells are mostly small-n and flagged with label error and small-sample limits. Full text was cut in the retrieved excerpt.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Play-type PPP comparison using initiation_type-based labels
failed_approaches.why: Foul-ending possessions leaked into OTHER and inflated PPP, and initiation_type mapped only 0.7% of possessions to a real play type.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Sequence-level PPP by inferred play type before the classifier was rewritten
failed_approaches.why: Assisted flag existed only on makes, so SPOT_UP showed 2.83 PPP (artifact); rewrite gave about 1.16.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Play-type label accuracy and distribution audit
failed_approaches.why: Overall FAIL with OTHER 20.2%, 40.8% low-confidence labels, DRIVE foul-draw rate far below benchmark, and identity checks failing; labeled tool_eval_fail with LABEL_ERROR, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD and SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER risks recorded.
Final FAIL: PULL_UP shares near zero for many teams, team identity FAIL, and 82.8% of PNR labels proxy_calibrated.
Confident label rates of 14.9% and 3.3%; switches_on unpopulated; recorded as untestable and failed_gate.

evidence_establishes: The derived play-type labels (DRIVE, PNR, OTHER, PULL_UP) have documented systematic errors in this project: foul leakage, OTHER inflation, PULL_UP near zero for many teams, identity failures, and a high share of proxy-calibrated PNR labels.
Play-type PPP is sensitive to context: RS vs playoff contrasts differ materially for DRIVE and PNR (SF-APPS-011, recorded as supported).

Labeling constructions have previously produced artifactual PPP differences (SF-PAP-096, SF-CHT-025), so any sequence PPP difference from these labels must be treated as a candidate artifact until ruled out.
Same-player DRIVE-to-PNR sequence estimates (SF40) vary in sign and are based on small samples, so no stable sequence premium is established by the retrieved record.
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record tests the teammate DRIVE-before-PNR sequence effect on PNR PPP directly. The closest is SF40, whose teammate cell text was cut.
No retrieved record reports a CI, a power calculation, or a validated sequence effect for this question.
No retrieved record reports validated PNR or DRIVE labels for the 2022-23 to 2025-26 window, so label validity for this question is unknown.
Whether the effect holds after adjustment for shooter, defense, lineup, and context is not addressed.
own_inferences: The question is well-posed in principle: sequences can be built from raw action types and possession order without relying on the derived initiator labels, which would reduce reliance on the failed labeling pipeline.

Because PNR and DRIVE labels are the primary risk, a sequence test built on derived labels would likely reproduce artifacts seen in earlier families (foul leakage, OTHER inflation, proxy calibration).
Teammate sequences are a subset of possessions, so per-team and per-player cells will be small and the test is likely underpowered unless pooled across seasons and teams.
The predicted artifact share is high because the historical base rate for label-derived PPP results in this project is high.
uncertainties: The full text of FAM:SF40 was not read; the teammate sequence cells (for example J. Brown to J. Tatum DRIVE to PNR) are truncated in the retrieved excerpt. A read_family call could change the evidence, but was not made here.
Statuses for several records are not_hypothesis_test, descriptive, or inconclusive rather than formal results, so they do not test the question.
Sample sizes, CIs, and power are missing for most records (for example SF-APPS-011, SF-APPS-012), so effect magnitudes are not reliable for planning.
The number of possessions with a teammate DRIVE immediately preceding PNR in the 2022-23 to 2025-26 data is unknown and not established by any record.
2025-26 playoffs are partial until 2026-06-21, so they must be excluded from the primary test if the analysis date is 2026-06-14.

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieved records show repeated label-validity failures and artifacts in this project's derived play-type data, including foul leakage, OTHER inflation, PULL_UP near zero, and proxy-calibrated PNR labels. These failures make a direct test on the derived labels unreliable, so the decision moves from a conventional proceed to do_not_proceed until labels are validated, with a gated plan for a raw-sequence test.

blocking_constraints.text: The DRIVE and PNR labels come from a derived pipeline with recorded FAIL verdicts, 82.8% proxy-calibrated PNR labels, and foul leakage; the question cannot be tested on these labels without validation.
Teammate DRIVE-then-PNR sequences are a narrow subset of possessions; per-team and per-player cells are small, so the effect may not be estimable at useful power without pooling.
Shooter quality, defensive matchup, lineup, score, and clock all plausibly affect both sequence occurrence and PNR PPP; without adjustment the contrast is not interpretable.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests the teammate DRIVE-to-PNR sequence effect directly. SF40 covers related sequential premiums, with mixed signs and small samples, and its teammate cell text was cut. The label-audit records (SF-CHT-025, SF-APPM-014, SF-APPA-030) show the labels needed for the question are unreliable, which is why the question is only partly addressed.

risks.text: DRIVE and PNR labels have recorded FAIL verdicts and foul leakage; PNR labels are 82.8% proxy-calibrated (FAM:SF-APPA-030, FAM:SF-APPM-014).
PPP is computed from possession records whose labels are derived from the same play-by-play; the labeling construction can induce PPP differences (FAM:SF-PAP-096, FAM:SF-CHT-025).
Possession type labels built using the full possession outcome (for example assisted flag or foul outcome) can leak the result into the predictor (FAM:SF-PAP-096, FAM:SF-APPM-014).
Teammate DRIVE-to-PNR sequences occur rarely; cells by team or player are small (FAM:SF40 cells n=30-70).
No power calculation exists for the sequence contrast; prior records lack CIs and report small n (FAM:SF-APPS-011, FAM:SF40).
Shooter, defense, lineup, score, clock, and playoff context all affect PNR PPP and sequence frequency; RS vs playoff differences are large (FAM:SF-APPS-011).
Label-derived PPP results in this project have a high artifact rate, so a positive signal is more likely to be an artifact than a real effect.
Searching across play-type pairs, teams, and players produces many contrasts; SF40 shows opposite-sign cells for the same sequence type.
The 2025-26 regular season is complete only from 2026-04-13 and playoffs are partial before 2026-06-21, so data version and season coverage shift over time.
Defensive matchup and partial possession fields are used in context variables; unpopulated fields (switches_on in SF-APPS-058) indicate measure gaps.

design.estimand: Adjusted difference in mean PNR possession points (PPP) between PNR possessions preceded by a teammate DRIVE within the same offensive possession and matched PNR possessions without that sequence. This is the gated primary estimand, conditional on passing label validation.
design.unit: Offensive possession with a PNR initiator, with a binary indicator for a teammate DRIVE immediately preceding it. Labels are taken from raw action-type sequences with an explicit possession ordering, not from the derived initiation_type records.
design.sample: Regular season 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25, and 2025-26 (complete from 2026-04-13 only), plus playoffs 2022-23 through 2024-25 (complete). Exclude 2025-26 playoffs, which are partial as of 2026-06-14. Stage 0 gate: a validation sample of PNR and DRIVE labels, hand-checked against raw action types, with a foul-ending exclusion, must reach a pre-specified agreement threshold before the primary test runs.
design.power: Not established. Before data access, compute the minimum detectable effect for the expected sequence count with cluster-robust (team and game) variance, and report the detectable effect size. Do not claim power without this calculation.
design.controls: Adjust for shooter identity or quality (player fixed effects or prior PPP), defensive matchup strength, lineup, score margin, game clock and period, possession-start context, and season/playoff status. Cluster standard errors by game and team.
design.falsification: (1) Placebo sequence: DRIVE by an opponent immediately preceding PNR should show no PPP premium. (2) Reversed order: PNR-then-DRIVE sequences should show no premium. (3) Non-PNR baseline: the same DRIVE-preceding structure for SPOT_UP or PULL_UP should be compared. Any non-null placebo result counts against the sequence effect.
design.multiplicity: Single pre-registered primary contrast (pooled teammate DRIVE to PNR). Team-, player-, and season-level cells are exploratory and reported with Holm correction across the pre-specified family of cells.
design.decision_rule: Proceed to inference only if the label validation gate passes. Declare support only if the adjusted primary effect has a 95% CI excluding zero, the placebo and reversed-order contrasts are null, and the effect survives the label-validation sensitivity analysis. Declare artifact if the effect disappears under label validation or matches the foul-leakage or placebo pattern. Otherwise report inconclusive.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game play-by-play, substitution intervals, starters, matchup minutes, and box-score summaries, as of 2026-06-14. Regular season 2022-23 to 2025-26 (2025-26 complete from 2026-04-13); playoffs 2022-23 to 2024-25. Derived play-type possession records in the graph database are excluded from the primary test and used only as a comparison for label-agreement diagnostics.

methodological_questions: does a teammate drive before a pick-and-roll raise PNR points per possession
reliability and labeling error of derived play-type initiator records
confounding by shot quality, player quality, and possession context
args.query: teammate drive preceding pick-and-roll effect on PNR possession points per possession play-type labeling data quality

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Field guidance:
- historical_evidence and failed_approaches: only records returned by a tool, with the status as recorded; empty lists
  if nothing relevant was returned.
- testability.p_testable: probability that the question can be answered with the stated data at useful statistical power.
- prior_work.already_answered: whether retrieved earlier work already answered substantially the same question.
  Use "unknown" if no earlier work was retrieved. List identifiers you relied on in prior_work.cited.
- predicted_outcome: probabilities (summing to 1) of what a competent test of the question as posed would conclude:
  supported, rejected (adequately powered null), untestable (cannot be tested with this data), artifact (apparent
  effect produced by a flaw), uncertain (inconclusive or inadequately tested).
- decision: proceed, proceed_with_changes (state the changes in design), or do_not_proceed.
- design: a pre-registration-quality plan even if the decision is do_not_proceed (then describe the minimum viable test).
